newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Journalist says smuggled fake bomb into EU summit.
newsitem.headline: Journalist says smuggled fake bomb into EU summit.

text.p: A television journalist said on Thursday he had smuggled parts for a fake bomb past heavy security into the European Union summit in Amsterdam this week.
Koen Scharrenberg, who works for Dutch TV production company The Storms Factory, said he used the Internet computer network to obtain a false identity and find out how to make a bomb.
Scharrenberg, 41, said he carried a bag containing wax, paraffin, batteries, tape and a primitive ignition device past a summit security checkpoint on Monday.
He said the bag, also containing television equipment, was not searched.
"We could have been carrying a kilogram of (plastic explosive) Semtex," Scharrenberg said.
The parts were assembled and taken into the conference room of the Dutch central bank, where the leaders were gathered for a press briefing.
Scharrenberg conceded the fake bomb would not have detonated because some key ingredients were missing.
He said his actions, captured on film, highlighted how the Internet could be misused.
Police denied security at the summit had failed.
Amsterdam police spokesman Klaas Wilting said the items carried into the summit by the journalist were "okay" and did not constitute a threat.
"We're laughing about it this morning," he told Reuters.
Summit security has been criticised after environmental protestors disrupted the final news conference on Wednesday morning.
